import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.84

by V. P. Shunkov

a) Is every binary finite $2$-group of finite exponent locally finite?

b) The same question for $p$-groups for $p > 2$.

Here a group is *binary finite* if every two of its elements generate a finite
subgroup, a *$p$-group* is a group in which every element has order a power of
$p$, a group has *finite exponent* if there is a positive integer $n$ with
$g^n = 1$ for all its elements $g$, and a group is *locally finite* if every
finitely generated subgroup is finite.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.84»

/-- A group $G$ is *binary finite* if every two elements $x, y \in G$ generate a
finite subgroup $\langle x, y \rangle$. -/
def IsBinaryFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure ({x, y} : Set G))

/-- A group $G$ is *locally finite* if every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is
finite. -/
def IsLocallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

/-- A finite group is locally finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyFinite.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsLocallyFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A locally finite group is binary finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyFinite.isBinaryFinite {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsLocallyFinite G) :
    IsBinaryFinite G :=
  fun x y => h _ ((Subgroup.fg_iff _).2 ⟨{x, y}, rfl, (Set.finite_singleton y).insert x⟩)

/--
Is every binary finite $2$-group of finite exponent locally finite?

That is, if $G$ is a group in which every two elements generate a finite
subgroup, every element has order a power of $2$, and there is a positive
integer $n$ with $g^n = 1$ for all $g \in G$, must every finitely generated
subgroup of $G$ be finite?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.84».parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
      IsBinaryFinite G → IsPGroup 2 G → Monoid.ExponentExists G → IsLocallyFinite G := by
  sorry

/--
Is every binary finite $p$-group of finite exponent locally finite, for every prime
$p > 2$?

That is, for every prime $p > 2$, if $G$ is a group in which every two elements
generate a finite subgroup, every element has order a power of $p$, and there is
a positive integer $n$ with $g^n = 1$ for all $g \in G$, must every finitely
generated subgroup of $G$ be finite?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.84».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → 2 < p → ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
      IsBinaryFinite G → IsPGroup p G → Monoid.ExponentExists G → IsLocallyFinite G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.84»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The two-slot split (a: p = 2; b: all primes p > 2) matches the source text, and the notes' readings of 'binary finite', 'p-group', 'finite exponent' and 'locally finite' agree with Shunkov's standard terminology.
modeling_decisions: 'p-group' is formalized as Mathlib's IsPGroup p G, i.e. ∀ g, ∃ k, g ^ p ^ k = 1 (every element has order a power of p). For p prime this is the standard meaning of p-group for possibly infinite groups.

'Finite exponent' is formalized as Monoid.ExponentExists G (∃ n, 0 < n ∧ ∀ g, g ^ n = 1) with no constraint that n be a power of p; in a p-group this is automatic, so the hypothesis matches the source without adding an unstated restriction.
'Binary finite' is ∀ x y, the subgroup generated by {x, y} is finite; taking x = y also covers 1-generated subgroups, which is harmless (those are 2-generated too).
'Locally finite' uses Subgroup.FG (closure of a Finset) and Finite on the subgroup's coerced type; this is the standard 'every finitely generated subgroup is finite'.
Groups are quantified over G : Type (universe 0), following the convention in the existing Kourovka files (1_40, 1_74, 19_25, 20_76).
Part b) quantifies over all primes p with 2 < p (∀ p, p.Prime → 2 < p → ...), per the decomposition table, rather than fixing a single odd prime.

Two short proved API lemmas (IsLocallyFinite.of_finite, IsLocallyFinite.isBinaryFinite) were added as basic tests of the bespoke definitions, as CONTRIBUTING.md asks; they are tagged @[category API, AMS 20] and carry no sorry.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

namespace Kourovka.«9.84»

/-- A group $G$ is *binary finite* if any two elements $a, b \in G$ generate a finite
subgroup $\langle a, b \rangle$. -/
def IsBinaryFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ a b : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {a, b})

/-- A group $G$ is *locally finite* if every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is finite. -/
def IsLocallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A finite group is locally finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyFinite.of_finite [Finite G] : IsLocallyFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A locally finite group is binary finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyFinite.isBinaryFinite (h : IsLocallyFinite G) : IsBinaryFinite G :=
  fun a b => h _ ((Subgroup.fg_iff _).mpr ⟨{a, b}, rfl, Set.toFinite _⟩)
